negative_findings.description: Searches in uk and en for Ukrainian media publishing PSP/acquiring volume rankings analogous to bank profit league tables returned only bank-centric rankings (Minfin, Forbes, Mind, Opendatabot). Payments-side results coverage appears scattered across trade press (psm7.com) and NBU-derived news items rather than any recurring media ranking.

brief: Ukrainian business and financial media form a dense, fast, and largely open aggregation layer over bank disclosure: Minfin, Forbes Ukraine and Mind.ua each run methodology-backed recurring bank league tables, while Ekonomichna Pravda, Interfax-Ukraine, RBC-Ukraine, NV Business and FinClub push quarterly profit rankings within days of NBU data release. Interfax-Ukraine is the standout dual-purpose source — an English-language earnings wire plus a press-release channel that banks and PSPs use as a de-facto investor-relations distribution point. The main structural weakness is the payments side: no Ukrainian outlet appears to run a recurring PSP or acquiring league table, leaving psm7.com (PaySpace Magazine) as the only dedicated trade title and pushing payments financials back onto regulator and company sources. Almost everything here is indirect and traces to the same upstream NBU reporting, so the cell is best used for materiality signal, entity discovery and translation rather than as data of record; Opendatabot is the most useful pointer for jumping from a media table back to structured underlying figures.
